title: Dawn Breaks - The Long Night Ends
_note: The moment the Long Dusk ends - the Keystar caught, the Skyweave Crown complete, first light walking across Vesperholm. A one-statement arc the engine can hold under the dawn cinematic (loops, but built to be faded by the scene). SNES register per the area-music standard (strings/pad real chords, pluck harp, sparse bell, tri_bass o2 / pad o3 / lead o4 / bell o5, <=7 peak voices, era snes, render --engine chip). QUOTES, not new themes: bars 1-8 state the Vesper motif in A MINOR exactly as gleam-emotional's wistful half states it (lift E4->A4->B4, settle C5-natural->B4->A4 - the long dusk remembered, first fragmented/hushed, then complete); bars 9-12 are the TURN (the gleam-emotional minor->major pivot contour, here pivoting to the RELATIVE major so the dawn lands in C - the Tinderwick lullaby's home key); bars 13-20 reprise the Tinderwick 'Lantern Lullaby' / Vesper motif NOTE-FOR-NOTE in full C major (the dawnstead-a major reading: G3->C4->D4 lift ... E4->D4->C4 settle, the lift reaching G4), over Tinderwick's own music-box arp re-voiced as pluck harp; bars 21-24 coda - the lift finally reaching the sky (E4->G4->C5 ... up to E5), bell crowning C6, held radiant C major. Structure: HUSH (1-4, drone + motif fragment, near-silence) -> THE LAST DARK (5-8, the minor statement complete, harmonic-minor E dominant) -> THE TURN (9-12, brightening, first bell glint) -> THE BLOOM (13-20, the lullaby whole in daylight, full band + heartbeat drums) -> CODA (21-24, ringing home). 84 BPM, 4/4, A minor -> C major, 24 bars (~68s). Render --loops 1.

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: Bars 1-4: the Vesper lift FRAGMENT, hushed, answered by silence (the settle withheld - the night holding its breath). Bars 5-8: the full minor statement (gleam-emotional's wistful half, quoted). Bars 9-12: the turn - the line climbs and lands on the dominant with a G3 pickup. Bars 13-20: the Tinderwick lullaby reprised whole in C major (dawnstead-a bars 1-8, note-for-note). Bars 21-24: coda - the lift finally reaching the sky.

tracks.name: pad
tracks._note: The harmonic floor. Silent bar 1; a bare A-E open fifth creeps in (the dark, hollow), fills to Am; the minor half walks Am-F-Am-E(harmonic-minor dominant, the gleam-emotional colour); the turn brightens F-C-G-G; the bloom carries Tinderwick's real chords (C, C/G turnarounds, the Am leaning bar) and holds radiant C at the close.

tracks.name: harmony
tracks._note: Pluck harp - SILENT through the dark (bars 1-10), wakes as the light catches (11-12, a rising broken dominant), then plays Tinderwick's own music-box arpeggio (C-E-G-E eighths; A-C-E under the leaning bar; G-B-D under cadences) through the bloom. Rests on beat 4 of the bell bars so the glints ring clear (<=7 voices).

tracks.name: bass
tracks._note: A held low A drone through the hush (the night's weight), then gleam-emotional's minor root walk (A-F-A-E), the turn's F-C-G cadence, and Tinderwick's warm root-fifth hearth pulse through the bloom. Final bar a held tonic - contented, the dawn holding.

tracks.name: drums
tracks._note: Nothing at all until the bloom - the dark is unmeasured. From bar 13 the Tinderwick heartbeat (soft kick + brushy hat), gentle and present, like the world's pulse returning. No crash; the dawn arrives, it doesn't crash in.
